title: LangChain Architecture & LCEL Chain Patterns
description: LangChain is a framework designed to simplify creating applications using large language models (LLMs) through composable abstractions.
detailedExplanation: LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) uses the pipe operator (`|`) to compose Runnables into a declarative sequence. Core components include PromptTemplates, ChatModels (ChatOpenAI), OutputParsers (StringOutputParser, JsonOutputParser), and Memory modules (BufferMemory, SummaryMemory).
architectureFlow: User Prompt -> PromptTemplate.format() -> ChatOpenAI LLM -> StringOutputParser -> Parsed Response String
examples: ConversationChain with BufferMemory for session context persistence
Sequential Chains passing context outputs from chain A to chain B

interviewQuestions.question: What is LCEL in LangChain and what benefits does it provide?
interviewQuestions.answer: LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) is a declarative syntax using the pipe operator to compose Runnables. It provides uniform streaming, async support, batching, parallel execution, and telemetry out of the box.

interviewQuestions.question: Difference between BufferMemory and SummaryMemory in LangChain?
interviewQuestions.answer: BufferMemory stores raw past messages in a buffer array (can exceed context window). SummaryMemory uses an LLM to dynamically summarize past context as it grows, keeping token usage flat.

bestPractices: Use LCEL over legacy chain classes for better streaming and async compatibility
Always set temperature to low values (0.0 - 0.2) when expecting structured output
Use BaseOutputParser implementations to validate outputs automatically
commonMistakes: Unbounded memory buffers causing context window overflow
Not handling API error limits inside long chain invocations

title: LlamaIndex Data Ingestion & VectorStoreIndex Architecture
description: LlamaIndex is a data framework for LLM applications that provides structured data ingestion, indexing, and retrieval primitives.
detailedExplanation: LlamaIndex parses documents into Node chunks, embeds each node using vector embedding models, and constructs searchable indexes (VectorStoreIndex, SummaryIndex, TreeIndex). A RetrieverQueryEngine performs semantic retrieval and response synthesis.
architectureFlow: Raw PDF Document -> DocumentReader -> NodeParser (Chunks) -> Embedding Model -> VectorStoreIndex -> RetrieverQueryEngine -> Synthesized Response
examples: VectorStoreIndex query engine with custom similarityTopK

interviewQuestions.question: How does LlamaIndex differ from LangChain?
interviewQuestions.answer: LangChain is a general-purpose framework for building LLM apps (chains, agents, tools). LlamaIndex is specialized specifically for data ingestion, indexing, and advanced RAG retrieval over external documents.

bestPractices: Use appropriate NodeParser chunk sizes (e.g. 512 - 1024 tokens) matching your document structure
Persist vector indexes locally or to vector databases to avoid re-embedding files on restart
commonMistakes: Parsing huge PDF files synchronously on the main thread causing server freezes

title: CrewAI Multi-Agent Workflow & Orchestration Patterns
description: CrewAI is a framework for orchestrating autonomous multi-agent teams, allowing specialized agents to collaborate sequentially or hierarchically.
detailedExplanation: Agents are defined by Role, Goal, Backstory, and Tool access. Tasks specify expected outputs. In a Sequential workflow, Agent 1 completes Task 1 and passes its document output as input context to Agent 2 (e.g., Business Analyst -> Architect -> Developer -> QA).
architectureFlow: Project Prompt -> Business Analyst Agent -> System Architect Agent -> Frontend Dev Agent -> Backend Dev Agent -> QA Agent -> Project Summary
examples: Hostel Management System architectural blueprint workflow
Automated code review & refactoring multi-agent crew

interviewQuestions.question: Explain Sequential vs Hierarchical agent execution in CrewAI.
interviewQuestions.answer: Sequential execution runs agents step-by-step in order, feeding each previous agent's output as context to the next. Hierarchical execution uses a Manager Agent that dynamically delegates tasks to worker agents based on progress.

bestPractices: Give each agent a highly specific backstory and role to enforce specialized behavior
Set maximum iteration caps to prevent infinite feedback loops between agents
Keep context window clean by summarizing intermediate agent outputs
commonMistakes: Vague agent goals leading to duplicated work between agents

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Vector Stores & Embeddings
description: RAG enhances LLM responses by retrieving relevant factual context from vector databases using high-dimensional vector embeddings.
detailedExplanation: Text is converted into numerical vector embeddings (e.g. 1536-dimensional float arrays from OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). When a user asks a question, the question is embedded, and Nearest Neighbor Search (Cosine Similarity or HNSW) retrieves top matching chunks to augment the LLM system prompt.
architectureFlow: Document -> Chunking -> Embedding Model -> Vector DB -> User Query -> Query Embedding -> Cosine Similarity Search -> Top Chunks -> LLM -> Answer
examples: Hybrid search combining keyword BM25 and vector semantic search
Function Calling / Tool Calling with JSON schema tool selection

interviewQuestions.question: What is Cosine Similarity and how is it used in Vector Search?
interviewQuestions.answer: Cosine similarity measures the cosine of the angle between two vectors in multi-dimensional space, ranging from -1 to 1. In RAG, a similarity score near 1.0 means the query and document chunk share close semantic meaning regardless of length.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Tool Calling / Function Calling in LLMs?
interviewQuestions.answer: Tool Calling allows LLMs to return structured JSON specifying a tool function to invoke (e.g. calculator(expression)) rather than text, enabling LLMs to interact with external APIs, databases, and code execution environments.

bestPractices: Use chunk overlap (10-20%) to preserve sentence boundary context
Re-rank retrieved context using Cross-Encoders (e.g. Cohere Rerank) for highest accuracy
Low temperature (0.0-0.2) for RAG responses to avoid hallucinating beyond retrieved context
commonMistakes: Using wrong embedding model during query retrieval mismatching indexing model
Extremely large chunk size diluting specific answers
